steps.message:
Item 054 on the verification register for Birchwood Village Expansion, Package A has to close before 07/20/2026. It covers the slab-on-grade fill compaction testing Vantree ran on 07/08/2026 and their Field Density Report SF-26-0708, issued the next day.

Work those results against Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, and give me an acceptance determination. State the acceptance basis you are using, the limits it produces, and what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.

Cover the testing as well as the results. I want to know whether what was done and recorded is enough to support the determination under that section, and what has to be in hand before anything is built on this fill.

Two files are attached: Fill_Placement_Records_BlockA_SlabOnGrade.xlsx, the Contractor's placement log for this fill, and Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Record_TEMPLATE.docx, our house format for a materials acceptance record. Use the template and save the finished record as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx.

                                       SECTION 31 20 00
                                         EARTH MOVING

                        Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A
                                      Thornbury State University

          Structural Engineer of Record: Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC
                            812 East Broad Street, Columbus, OH 43205

     Revision: Rev.3 | Issue Date: 03/06/2026 | Supersedes: Rev.2 (issued 11/14/2025)



PART 1    GENERAL

   1.1 SUMMARY
   A. Section Includes:
         1. Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
            pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
         2.    Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
              building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
         3. Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
         4. Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
   B. Related Sections:
         1.    Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
              envelope.
         2. Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
         3. Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
            subgrade.

   1.2 REFERENCES
   A.    Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
         cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
         1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
              only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
         2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
              Package A structural fill.
         3. ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
            and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
            method.
         4.     ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
              (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content




                                         31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6
                                             Earth Moving
           when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
     5. ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
        Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
        Engineer of Record.

1.3 DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
     beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
     meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B. Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.    Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
     maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.    Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
     content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.    Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
     whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
     by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.

1.4 QUALITY ASSURANCE
A. Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
   Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
   directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
   lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.    Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
     documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
     shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
     the start of each testing day.
C.     Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
     moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
     determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
     the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
     D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
     accepted.

1.5 SUBMITTALS
A. Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
     1.    Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
          Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
     2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
          D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
     3.    Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
          passes.
B. During placement, submit daily:




                                     31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
          1. Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
            density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
            and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
            deviation from optimum.

   1.6 SEQUENCING
   A.     No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
         presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
   B.     No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
         accepted per Article 3.4.

PART 2    PRODUCTS

   2.1 STRUCTURAL FILL
   A.     Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
         D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
   B.     Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
         the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
   C.     Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
         particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
   D.    Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
         shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
         Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
         which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.

   2.2 COMMON FILL
   A. Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
      frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.

   2.3 CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
   A. Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
      placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.

PART 3    EXECUTION

   3.1 EXAMINATION
   A.     Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
         that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
         Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.

   3.2 SUBGRADE PREPARATION
   A. Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
      structural fill.
   B. Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
      approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present




                                          31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
                                              Earth Moving
      to witness the proof roll.
C.    Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
     Section.

3.3 PLACEMENT
A. Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.    Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
     the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.    Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
     requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.     Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
     precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
     3.4.B.

3.4 COMPACTION
A. Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
   Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
   moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
   (self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
   structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
   within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
   Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
   Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
   placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
   intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
   general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
   compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
   compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
   shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B. Acceptance Criteria.
             Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
             95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
             placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
             of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
             be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
             D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
             5,000 sf per lift.

C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
     not satisfied at any test location:
     1.    The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
          recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
     2.    Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
          criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.




                                     31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
      3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
          compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.    Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
     location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
     density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
     test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
     density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.

3.5 BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A. Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
   specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
   place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.    Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
     thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C. Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
   structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.

3.6 SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
     0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.    Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
     constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
     predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
     Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
     written disposition is issued.
C.    Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
     be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.

[021] 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
[022] The acceptance basis applied in this review is the laboratory reference compaction standard established for Package A structural fill by Specification Section 31 20 00 — Earth Moving, Rev.3, namely ASTM D1557 Method C (Modified Proctor). The governing specification articles are:
[023] •  Article 1.2.A.2 designates ASTM D1557 as the “Governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill”; Article 1.2.A.1 designates ASTM D698 for “historical borrow characterization only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.”
[024] •  Article 1.3.E defines “Placed Material” as the soil actually placed, whose maximum dry density and optimum moisture have been established by ASTM D1557 Method C testing prior to placement.
[025] •  Article 1.4.C (Placed-Material Correspondence) requires that the denominators for any test location be those determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location.
[026] •  Article 2.1.D requires the Laboratory to determine maximum dry density and optimum moisture by ASTM D1557 Method C for each source and each material change prior to placement; those values are the denominators for Article 3.4.B.
[027] •  Article 3.4.B sets the acceptance criteria: dry density not less than 95% of the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density for the placed material, AND moisture content within −1% to +2% of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must be satisfied at each test location. Field density is measured per ASTM D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission) at one test per 5,000 sf per lift.
[028] •  Article 3.4.D requires that both criteria be independently satisfied at each test location against the D1557 Method C denominators; no test location may be accepted on density alone or on moisture alone.
[029] •  Article 3.7.A.1 sets testing frequency: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of area.
[030] •  Article 3.7.B requires each report to identify the D1557 Method C denominators, measured dry density, measured moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation from optimum, and the accept/reject disposition against Article 3.4.B.
[031] •  Article 3.7.C provides that any lift for which the D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually placed is non-conforming and shall be reworked per Article 3.4.C.
[032] The laboratory values establishing this basis for the Block A slab-on-grade fill are those of Vantree Report VMT-25-0918-P04 (ASTM D1557 Method C, dated 09/18/2025): maximum dry density γd,max = 128.4 pcf and optimum moisture content wopt = 9.2%, for the Package A structural fill borrow (Larchwood Pit; USCS SM/SW-SM). That report states expressly that its results constitute the laboratory reference values for percent-compaction determinations on Package A structural fill, that it supersedes any earlier Proctor result for structural fill on Package A, and that field compaction acceptance shall be evaluated against these values in accordance with Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B; it also gives, for reference, 95% of maximum dry density = 122.0 pcf.
[033] This basis is established for the fill under review by the following record: (a) the Specification articles above; (b) the D1557 laboratory report VMT-25-0918-P04 itself, which names Section 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B as its specification reference; (c) the Contractor’s placement record RB-FPR-BA-2026, which carries VMT-25-0918-P04 as its “Governing Proctor reference” and states the compaction acceptance basis as “Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B”; and (d) Verification Register Items 012 (closed 09/22/2025, confirming the Package A structural fill Modified Proctor on file) and 027 (closed 03/13/2026, confirming that the dual density and moisture criteria of Article 3.4.B bind independently).
[034] Acceptance limits produced by this basis.  Minimum acceptable in-place dry density = 95% × 128.4 pcf = 121.98 pcf (reported as 122.0 pcf). Acceptable moisture-content window = wopt −1% to +2% = 8.2% to 11.2%. Both limits must be met independently at each test location; density alone is not sufficient.
[035] Accordingly, the acceptance basis applied in this review is ASTM D1557 Method C (VMT-25-0918-P04), and not the ASTM D698 Method A curve (VMT-2024-0403-P1B) that Field Density Report SF-26-0708 actually used as its “Reference Proctor.”
[037] 4.  FINDINGS
[038] Finding 1 — Governing acceptance basis and limits.  The acceptance basis for Package A structural fill is ASTM D1557 Method C. The Block A slab-on-grade fill was placed from the Package A structural fill borrow characterized in Vantree Report VMT-25-0918-P04 (γd,max 128.4 pcf, wopt 9.2%; sealed 09/18/2025). The acceptance limits are minimum dry density 122.0 pcf and moisture content 8.2%–11.2%, both required at each test location. (Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.2.A.2, 1.3.E, 2.1.D, 3.4.B, 3.4.D; VMT-25-0918-P04, Sections 6–7; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Cover and Note 5; Register Items 012, 027.)
[039] Finding 2 — Wrong laboratory reference used in the field density report.  SF-26-0708, Section 3 (“Reference Proctor”), reports percent compaction relative to ASTM D698 Method A, γd,max = 118.6 pcf, wopt = 12.1%, “Curve of Record Vantree Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B (dated 04/03/2024).” That curve is the Phase 1 Wexford Ridge Borrow characterization — a CL-ML silty clay (LL 32, PL 21, PI 11, 68% passing the No. 200 sieve) tested with standard effort (12,375 ft-lbf/ft³) in April 2024 for “Phase 1 off-site borrow source characterization” (Proctor D698 report VMT-2024-0403-P1B, Sections 1–2 and 6). Specification Article 1.2.A.1 expressly limits ASTM D698 to “historical borrow characterization only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.” The material actually placed is the Package A structural fill borrow characterized by the D1557 Method C curve (a well-graded SM/SW-SM granular fill), per the Contractor’s placement record. The denominators used in SF-26-0708 therefore do not correspond to the material actually placed, contrary to Articles 1.4.C, 2.1.D, and 3.7.C. The reported percent-compaction values (105.2, 104.1, 103.6, 106.3%) are computed against the 118.6 pcf D698 denominator and are not the values required by the Specification. (SF-26-0708 Sections 3 and 5; VMT-2024-0403-P1B Sections 1–2, 6; VMT-25-0918-P04 Sections 3, 7; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 1.2.A.1–2, 1.4.C, 2.1.D, 3.7.C.)
[040] Finding 3 — Moisture criterion not evaluated.  Article 3.4.B requires both a density criterion and a moisture criterion (moisture within −1% to +2% of the D1557 optimum), and Article 3.4.D prohibits accepting any test location on density alone. SF-26-0708 does not evaluate moisture against any acceptance window. Its Section 4 (“Specification Requirement”) restates only the density criterion (“minimum in-place dry density … not less than 95 percent of the maximum dry density determined by the reference Proctor”) and omits the moisture criterion. The “Pass/Fail” column of the tabulation reflects density only; no moisture deviation from optimum is reported, and no moisture disposition is given. This does not satisfy Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, or 3.7.B (which requires the report to state moisture deviation from optimum and disposition against Article 3.4.B). (SF-26-0708 Sections 4, 5, and 6; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, 3.7.B.)
[041] Finding 4 — Recomputation against the governing D1557 Method C basis.  Using the governing denominators (γd,max 128.4 pcf, wopt 9.2%), the four tests evaluate as set out below (minimum dry density 122.0 pcf; moisture window 8.2%–11.2%; both criteria required at each location):
[042] All four locations meet the density criterion. FD-15 (Grid D-5) and FD-16 (Grid F-4) meet both criteria. FD-14 (Grid B-3, moisture 6.1%) and FD-17 (Grid G-2, moisture 5.8%) fail the moisture criterion — both are on the dry side, below the 8.2% lower limit. Per Article 3.4.C, isolated failing tests may not be averaged with passing tests; the affected areas must be reworked and retested, and both criteria must be satisfied on the retest. (SF-26-0708 Section 5 tabulation; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.C, 3.4.D.)
[043] Finding 5 — The report’s PASS dispositions are unsupported under either basis.  For completeness, if the moisture criterion had been applied against the report’s own D698 denominator (wopt 12.1%; window 11.1%–14.1%), all four tests (6.1%, 9.8%, 10.4%, 5.8%) would fail the moisture criterion. Under neither the governing basis nor the report’s erroneous basis do the recorded data support the report’s all-PASS disposition. The omission of the moisture criterion left the dry-side non-conformances at FD-14 and FD-17 unaddressed. (SF-26-0708 Sections 3 and 5; Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B.)
[044] Finding 6 — Field test execution was otherwise compliant.  The field testing was executed in accordance with the Specification’s method, calibration, personnel, and frequency requirements. The test method was ASTM D6938 nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode, 6-in probe depth, 60-second count (Article 3.4.B). The gauge (Troxler 3440, S/N 34-047162) carried an annual factory calibration dated 02/06/2026 and was standard-count checked at the site on 07/08/2026 before the first test, within manufacturer tolerance (Article 1.4.B). The work was performed by the Owner’s independent laboratory under PE supervision (J. Rennick, technician; K. Halbrenn, laboratory manager; sealed by Talia Brennard, PE), satisfying Articles 1.4.A and 1.4.B. Four tests were taken on Lift 6 at finished grade El. 748.6 across the 11,400-sf pad; Article 3.7.A.1 requires one test per 5,000 sf per lift and not fewer than three per lift — four tests satisfies both. The Contractor’s placement record corroborates the sequence: six lifts placed 06/22/2026–07/08/2026 at 8-in loose / 7.2-in compacted thickness (within the 12-in loose maximum of Article 3.3.A), on a subgrade proof-rolled 06/18/2026 and accepted in writing (Thelbridge memo TPM-26-063), following a production test strip on 06/19/2026 that established six coverage passes. The deficiency is therefore confined to the report’s evaluation, not to the field test execution. The raw field data are usable and, properly evaluated against the governing basis, support the determination in Finding 4. (SF-26-0708 Sections 1 and 2; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Daily Placement Log and Notes 2, 3, 6; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 1.4, 3.3.A, 3.4.B, 3.7.A.1.)
[045] Finding 7 — Placed-material correspondence to be confirmed.  Article 1.4.C requires the denominators to correspond to the material actually placed. The governing D1557 report (VMT-25-0918-P04) identifies its borrow source as the “Larchwood Pit — Package A structural fill,” while the Contractor’s placement record identifies the fill as drawn from the “stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse per RFI 079.” The corrected report should expressly reconcile these source identifications — confirming the stockpile material is the Larchwood Pit material characterized by VMT-25-0918-P04, or, if the placed material differs materially, performing a new ASTM D1557 Method C determination on the actual placed material before acceptance (Articles 1.4.C and 2.1.D). This is a documentation/reconciliation item; it does not alter the conclusion that the D698 curve used in SF-26-0708 is the wrong material and wrong standard. (VMT-25-0918-P04 Sections 1–2; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Cover and Note 4; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 1.4.C, 2.1.D.)
[046] Finding 8 — Schedule and hold-point context.  The Contractor’s pour-readiness notification of 07/14/2026 lists “Slab-on-grade fill compaction report SF-26-0708 … all four tests exceed 95% requirement” among the results asserted compliant for the 07/22/2026 placement. That assertion rests on the report’s erroneous D698 evaluation and its omission of the moisture criterion; it is not supported by the governing basis, under which two of the four tests fail. The Owner’s directive of 07/06/2026 requires Thelbridge written verification before any permanent work proceeds and states the Owner “would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work.” Item 054 accordingly cannot be closed on the present record. (Kendrow email 07/14/2026, item (b); Marlbeck email 07/06/2026; Verification Register — Schedule.)
[048] 5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
[049] Determination: REJECTED.  The slab-on-grade fill compaction of Lift 6 (Block A, finished grade El. 748.6) as documented in Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 is not accepted under Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B. Two independent non-conformances are established: (1) the report evaluated density against ASTM D698 Method A (VMT-2024-0403-P1B), a Phase 1 borrow-characterization curve of a different material that the Specification expressly excludes as the acceptance basis, rather than the governing ASTM D1557 Method C curve (VMT-25-0918-P04) for the placed Package A structural fill (Articles 1.2.A, 1.4.C, 2.1.D, 3.7.C); and (2) the report did not evaluate the moisture criterion and purported to accept all four tests on density alone, contrary to Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, and 3.7.B. Evaluated against the governing D1557 Method C basis (minimum dry density 122.0 pcf; moisture 8.2%–11.2%), all four tests meet the density criterion, but FD-14 (Grid B-3, moisture 6.1%) and FD-17 (Grid G-2, moisture 5.8%) fail the moisture criterion. The fill as documented therefore does not satisfy the Specification.
[050] The field test execution (method ASTM D6938 direct transmission, gauge calibration and standard-count, PE-supervised Owner’s laboratory, and test frequency of four tests over 11,400 sf) complied with the Specification; the deficiency is confined to the report’s evaluation. The raw field data are usable and, properly evaluated, support this determination.

3. BASIS OF REVIEW
The acceptance basis applied in this review is the laboratory reference compaction
standard established for Package A structural fill by Specification Section 31 20 00 —
Earth Moving, Rev.3, namely ASTM D1557 Method C (Modified Proctor). The governing
specification articles are:
• Article 1.2.A.2 designates ASTM D1557 as the “Governing laboratory reference for
   Package A structural fill”; Article 1.2.A.1 designates ASTM D698 for “historical
   borrow characterization only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.”
• Article 1.3.E defines “Placed Material” as the soil actually placed, whose maximum dry
   density and optimum moisture have been established by ASTM D1557 Method C
   testing prior to placement.
• Article 1.4.C (Placed-Material Correspondence) requires that the denominators for any
   test location be those determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually
   placed at that location.
• Article 2.1.D requires the Laboratory to determine maximum dry density and optimum
   moisture by ASTM D1557 Method C for each source and each material change prior to
   placement; those values are the denominators for Article 3.4.B.
• Article 3.4.B sets the acceptance criteria: dry density not less than 95% of the ASTM
   D1557 Method C maximum dry density for the placed material, AND moisture content
   within −1% to +2% of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test.
   Both criteria must be satisfied at each test location. Field density is measured per
   ASTM D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission) at one test per 5,000 sf per lift.
• Article 3.4.D requires that both criteria be independently satisfied at each test location
   against the D1557 Method C denominators; no test location may be accepted on
   density alone or on moisture alone.
• Article 3.7.A.1 sets testing frequency: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, and
   not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of area.
• Article 3.7.B requires each report to identify the D1557 Method C denominators,
   measured dry density, measured moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation
   from optimum, and the accept/reject disposition against Article 3.4.B.
• Article 3.7.C provides that any lift for which the D1557 Method C denominators used in
   reporting do not correspond to the material actually placed is non-conforming and
   shall be reworked per Article 3.4.C.
The laboratory values establishing this basis for the Block A slab-on-grade fill are those of
Vantree Report VMT-25-0918-P04 (ASTM D1557 Method C, dated 09/18/2025): maximum
dry density γd,max = 128.4 pcf and optimum moisture content wopt = 9.2%, for the
Package A structural fill borrow (Larchwood Pit; USCS SM/SW-SM). That report states
expressly that its results constitute the laboratory reference values for percent-
compaction determinations on Package A structural fill, that it supersedes any earlier
Proctor result for structural fill on Package A, and that field compaction acceptance shall
be evaluated against these values in accordance with Specification Section 31 20 00,
Article 3.4.B; it also gives, for reference, 95% of maximum dry density = 122.0 pcf.
 ########## PAGE 3 ##########
This basis is established for the fill under review by the following record: (a) the
Specification articles above; (b) the D1557 laboratory report VMT-25-0918-P04 itself,
which names Section 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B as its specification reference; (c) the
Contractor’s placement record RB-FPR-BA-2026, which carries VMT-25-0918-P04 as its
“Governing Proctor reference” and states the compaction acceptance basis as
“Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B”; and (d) Verification Register Items 012
(closed 09/22/2025, confirming the Package A structural fill Modified Proctor on file) and
027 (closed 03/13/2026, confirming that the dual density and moisture criteria of Article
3.4.B bind independently).
Acceptance limits produced by this basis. Minimum acceptable in-place dry density =
95% × 128.4 pcf = 121.98 pcf (reported as 122.0 pcf). Acceptable moisture-content
window = wopt −1% to +2% = 8.2% to 11.2%. Both limits must be met independently at
each test location; density alone is not sufficient.
Accordingly, the acceptance basis applied in this review is ASTM D1557 Method C
(VMT-25-0918-P04), and not the ASTM D698 Method A curve (VMT-2024-0403-P1B) that
Field Density Report SF-26-0708 actually used as its “Reference Proctor.”


4. FINDINGS
Finding 1 — Governing acceptance basis and limits. The acceptance basis for
Package A structural fill is ASTM D1557 Method C. The Block A slab-on-grade fill was
placed from the Package A structural fill borrow characterized in Vantree Report VMT-25-
0918-P04 (γd,max 128.4 pcf, wopt 9.2%; sealed 09/18/2025). The acceptance limits are
minimum dry density 122.0 pcf and moisture content 8.2%–11.2%, both required at each
test location. (Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.2.A.2, 1.3.E, 2.1.D, 3.4.B, 3.4.D; VMT-25-
0918-P04, Sections 6–7; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Cover and Note 5; Register Items 012, 027.)
Finding 2 — Wrong laboratory reference used in the field density report. SF-26-
0708, Section 3 (“Reference Proctor”), reports percent compaction relative to ASTM D698
Method A, γd,max = 118.6 pcf, wopt = 12.1%, “Curve of Record Vantree Report
VMT-2024-0403-P1B (dated 04/03/2024).” That curve is the Phase 1 Wexford Ridge
Borrow characterization — a CL-ML silty clay (LL 32, PL 21, PI 11, 68% passing the No.
200 sieve) tested with standard effort (12,375 ft-lbf/ft³) in April 2024 for “Phase 1 off-site
borrow source characterization” (Proctor D698 report VMT-2024-0403-P1B, Sections 1–2
and 6). Specification Article 1.2.A.1 expressly limits ASTM D698 to “historical borrow
characterization only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.” The material
actually placed is the Package A structural fill borrow characterized by the D1557 Method
C curve (a well-graded SM/SW-SM granular fill), per the Contractor’s placement record.
The denominators used in SF-26-0708 therefore do not correspond to the material actually
placed, contrary to Articles 1.4.C, 2.1.D, and 3.7.C. The reported percent-compaction
values (105.2, 104.1, 103.6, 106.3%) are computed against the 118.6 pcf D698
denominator and are not the values required by the Specification. (SF-26-0708 Sections 3
and 5; VMT-2024-0403-P1B Sections 1–2, 6; VMT-25-0918-P04 Sections 3, 7; Spec 31 20
00 Articles 1.2.A.1–2, 1.4.C, 2.1.D, 3.7.C.)
Finding 3 — Moisture criterion not evaluated. Article 3.4.B requires both a density
criterion and a moisture criterion (moisture within −1% to +2% of the D1557 optimum),
and Article 3.4.D prohibits accepting any test location on density alone. SF-26-0708 does
not evaluate moisture against any acceptance window. Its Section 4 (“Specification
Requirement”) restates only the density criterion (“minimum in-place dry density … not
less than 95 percent of the maximum dry density determined by the reference Proctor”)
and omits the moisture criterion. The “Pass/Fail” column of the tabulation reflects density
only; no moisture deviation from optimum is reported, and no moisture disposition is
given. This does not satisfy Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, or 3.7.B (which requires the report to
 ########## PAGE 4 ##########
state moisture deviation from optimum and disposition against Article 3.4.B). (SF-26-0708
Sections 4, 5, and 6; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, 3.7.B.)
Finding 4 — Recomputation against the governing D1557 Method C basis. Using
the governing denominators (γd,max 128.4 pcf, wopt 9.2%), the four tests evaluate as set
out below (minimum dry density 122.0 pcf; moisture window 8.2%–11.2%; both criteria
required at each location):
  Test     Dry density   Moistur        %          Density       Moisture        Result
              (pcf)       e (%)    compaction    (≥122.0 pcf)   (8.2–11.2%)
                                     (D1557)
 FD-14        124.8        6.1         97.2          PASS        FAIL (below      FAIL
                                                                     8.2)
 FD-15        123.5         9.8        96.2          PASS           PASS         PASS
 FD-16        122.9        10.4        95.7          PASS           PASS         PASS
 FD-17        126.1         5.8        98.2          PASS        FAIL (below     FAIL
                                                                     8.2)
All four locations meet the density criterion. FD-15 (Grid D-5) and FD-16 (Grid F-4) meet
both criteria. FD-14 (Grid B-3, moisture 6.1%) and FD-17 (Grid G-2, moisture 5.8%) fail
the moisture criterion — both are on the dry side, below the 8.2% lower limit. Per Article
3.4.C, isolated failing tests may not be averaged with passing tests; the affected areas
must be reworked and retested, and both criteria must be satisfied on the retest. (SF-26-
0708 Section 5 tabulation; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.C, 3.4.D.)
Finding 5 — The report’s PASS dispositions are unsupported under either basis.
For completeness, if the moisture criterion had been applied against the report’s own
D698 denominator (wopt 12.1%; window 11.1%–14.1%), all four tests (6.1%, 9.8%, 10.4%,
5.8%) would fail the moisture criterion. Under neither the governing basis nor the report’s
erroneous basis do the recorded data support the report’s all-PASS disposition. The
omission of the moisture criterion left the dry-side non-conformances at FD-14 and FD-17
unaddressed. (SF-26-0708 Sections 3 and 5; Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B.)
Finding 6 — Field test execution was otherwise compliant. The field testing was
executed in accordance with the Specification’s method, calibration, personnel, and
frequency requirements. The test method was ASTM D6938 nuclear gauge, direct-
transmission mode, 6-in probe depth, 60-second count (Article 3.4.B). The gauge (Troxler
3440, S/N 34-047162) carried an annual factory calibration dated 02/06/2026 and was
standard-count checked at the site on 07/08/2026 before the first test, within
manufacturer tolerance (Article 1.4.B). The work was performed by the Owner’s
independent laboratory under PE supervision (J. Rennick, technician; K. Halbrenn,
laboratory manager; sealed by Talia Brennard, PE), satisfying Articles 1.4.A and 1.4.B.
Four tests were taken on Lift 6 at finished grade El. 748.6 across the 11,400-sf pad;
Article 3.7.A.1 requires one test per 5,000 sf per lift and not fewer than three per lift —
four tests satisfies both. The Contractor’s placement record corroborates the sequence:
six lifts placed 06/22/2026–07/08/2026 at 8-in loose / 7.2-in compacted thickness (within
the 12-in loose maximum of Article 3.3.A), on a subgrade proof-rolled 06/18/2026 and
accepted in writing (Thelbridge memo TPM-26-063), following a production test strip on
06/19/2026 that established six coverage passes. The deficiency is therefore confined to
the report’s evaluation, not to the field test execution. The raw field data are usable and,
properly evaluated against the governing basis, support the determination in Finding 4.
(SF-26-0708 Sections 1 and 2; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Daily Placement Log and Notes 2, 3, 6;
Spec 31 20 00 Articles 1.4, 3.3.A, 3.4.B, 3.7.A.1.)
Finding 7 — Placed-material correspondence to be confirmed. Article 1.4.C
requires the denominators to correspond to the material actually placed. The governing
D1557 report (VMT-25-0918-P04) identifies its borrow source as the “Larchwood Pit —
Package A structural fill,” while the Contractor’s placement record identifies the fill as
drawn from the “stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse per RFI 079.” The
 ########## PAGE 5 ##########
corrected report should expressly reconcile these source identifications — confirming the
stockpile material is the Larchwood Pit material characterized by VMT-25-0918-P04, or, if
the placed material differs materially, performing a new ASTM D1557 Method C
determination on the actual placed material before acceptance (Articles 1.4.C and 2.1.D).
This is a documentation/reconciliation item; it does not alter the conclusion that the D698
curve used in SF-26-0708 is the wrong material and wrong standard. (VMT-25-0918-P04
Sections 1–2; RB-FPR-BA-2026 Cover and Note 4; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 1.4.C, 2.1.D.)
Finding 8 — Schedule and hold-point context. The Contractor’s pour-readiness
notification of 07/14/2026 lists “Slab-on-grade fill compaction report SF-26-0708 … all four
tests exceed 95% requirement” among the results asserted compliant for the 07/22/2026
placement. That assertion rests on the report’s erroneous D698 evaluation and its
omission of the moisture criterion; it is not supported by the governing basis, under which
two of the four tests fail. The Owner’s directive of 07/06/2026 requires Thelbridge written
verification before any permanent work proceeds and states the Owner “would rather
delay the pour than release non-conforming work.” Item 054 accordingly cannot be closed
on the present record. (Kendrow email 07/14/2026, item (b); Marlbeck email 07/06/2026;
Verification Register — Schedule.)


5. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Determination: REJECTED. The slab-on-grade fill compaction of Lift 6 (Block A,
finished grade El. 748.6) as documented in Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 is
not accepted under Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B. Two independent non-
conformances are established: (1) the report evaluated density against ASTM D698
Method A (VMT-2024-0403-P1B), a Phase 1 borrow-characterization curve of a different
material that the Specification expressly excludes as the acceptance basis, rather than the
governing ASTM D1557 Method C curve (VMT-25-0918-P04) for the placed Package A
structural fill (Articles 1.2.A, 1.4.C, 2.1.D, 3.7.C); and (2) the report did not evaluate the
moisture criterion and purported to accept all four tests on density alone, contrary to
Articles 3.4.B, 3.4.D, and 3.7.B. Evaluated against the governing D1557 Method C basis
(minimum dry density 122.0 pcf; moisture 8.2%–11.2%), all four tests meet the density
criterion, but FD-14 (Grid B-3, moisture 6.1%) and FD-17 (Grid G-2, moisture 5.8%) fail
the moisture criterion. The fill as documented therefore does not satisfy the Specification.
The field test execution (method ASTM D6938 direct transmission, gauge calibration and
standard-count, PE-supervised Owner’s laboratory, and test frequency of four tests over
11,400 sf) complied with the Specification; the deficiency is confined to the report’s
evaluation. The raw field data are usable and, properly evaluated, support this
determination.
Action required before anything is built on this fill — i.e., before the capillary
break course (Article 2.3) or the slab-on-grade is placed on the completed fill pad:
1. Issue a corrected (or supplemental) field density report for Lift 6 that (a) uses the
    ASTM D1557 Method C denominators from VMT-25-0918-P04 (γd,max 128.4 pcf, wopt
    9.2%) as the acceptance basis; (b) reconciles the placed-material source identification
    (Larchwood Pit vs. stockpile north of Block C / RFI 079) and confirms the
    denominators correspond to the material actually placed, or performs a new D1557
    Method C determination if the placed material differs materially (Articles 1.4.C,
    2.1.D); and (c) for each test location reports the D1557 Method C denominators,
    measured dry density, measured moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation
    from optimum, and the accept/reject disposition against both criteria (Article 3.7.B).
2. Rework the failing locations — FD-14 (Grid B-3) and FD-17 (Grid G-2), and the lift areas
    they represent — per Article 3.4.C: scarify, moisture-condition to bring in-place
    moisture within 8.2%–11.2%, recompact, and retest. Both the density and moisture

    passing tests. (The dry-side readings are consistent with the surface-moisture-loss
    conditions noted by the field engineer on 06/26 and 06/30; the moisture-conditioning-

3. Provide additional confirmation tests across Lift 6 sufficient to demonstrate that the

The deliverable is complete and verified on disk.

## Summary

**Deliverable:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` — a Materials Acceptance Record built on the Thelbridge house template, verified to open correctly (python-docx) and render cleanly to a 6-page Letter PDF with the recomputation table intact. No leftover template instruction text remains.

**Determination: REJECTED** — Verification Register Item 054, slab-on-grade fill compaction (Lift 6, Block A; Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708).

- **Basis & limits:** ASTM D1557 Method C (VMT-25-0918-P04; γd,max = 128.4 pcf, wopt = 9.2%) per Spec 31 20 00 — producing minimum dry density 122.0 pcf and moisture window 8.2%–11.2%, both required independently at each location. Established for this fill by the spec articles, the D1557 report itself, the Contractor's placement log RB-FPR-BA-2026, and Register Items 012/027.
- **Results:** SF-26-0708 used the wrong curve (ASTM D698 Method A — a Phase 1 CL-ML clay the spec expressly excludes) and never evaluated the moisture criterion. Recomputed on the correct basis, all four tests pass density but FD-14 (6.1%) and FD-17 (5.8%) fail moisture; FD-15 and FD-16 pass.
- **Testing:** Field execution was compliant (ASTM D6938, calibrated/standard-counted gauge, PE-sealed Owner's lab, frequency met); the deficiency is confined to the report's evaluation — the raw data support the rejection.
- **Before anything is built on the fill:** corrected report on the D1557 basis with moisture deviation and per-location disposition; rework/retest of FD-14 and FD-17; additional confirmation tests; Thelbridge written lift acceptance (Articles 1.6.B, 3.8) per the Owner's hold-point directive; fill protection until covered.

Item 054 is reported as not closed and not cleared for the 07/22/2026 hold-point on the present record.
